manifest.name: dsh-lan-access
manifest.author: icetea <cxxiao@zzu.edu.cn>
manifest.description: Open the DeepSeek Harness Web LAN access fences: serve on all interfaces, trust only the configured LAN authorities, and show a settings tab to choose them.

bundle.text:
# dsh-lan-access bundle patch — static composition (0.6.0).
#
# THE ROWS ARE CONFIGURED, NOT REWRITTEN. This bundle declares three things
# and performs no row updates at runtime:
#
#   1. `insert:` the single `lan-access` row — the plugin entry itself, and
#      the ONLY row dshmarket's toggle ever writes `disabled: true` onto
#      (market manages rows a package inserts, never top-level overrides).
#      Disabling the package therefore never touches an official row.
#
#   2. A top-level `webserver` override whose `host` is a loader `!!js`
#      expression: `0.0.0.0` only while the `lan-access` entry is enabled
#      AND the settings-tab toggle (`settings.yaml` lan-access.enabled) is
#      on; `127.0.0.1` (the official expression) otherwise. Market's
#      disable lands as a plain `disabled: true` on the entry before
#      activation, so the expression reads the final state with no race.
#      The bind is decided ONCE per boot: toggling the plugin only
#      starts/stops its fiber — the binding changes on the next restart,
#      exactly what the settings tab tells the user.
#
#   3. A top-level `connection` override that, while enabled (entry not
#      disabled AND the settings-tab toggle on), replaces the
#      browser-trust fence with the configured `accessHosts` (kept only in
#      the canonical form the fence's own `assertTrustedAuthority` accepts,
#      so a hand-edited invalid entry can never fail the row) — a non-empty
#      configuration IS the policy (strict fence, unchanged since 0.2.0);
#      with nothing configured it falls back to the deployment-derived
#      `webRuntime.trustedHosts`. It also applies the configured
#      session-cookie lifetime. While disabled both expressions return the
#      official ones, so --trusted-host deployments keep working.
#
# Overriding by id replaces the matched row's whole `config`, so each
# override restates every key the official row owns (the official rows live
# in @deepseek-ai/dsh-web-app/cordis.patch.yml); keys this file does not
# restate (`name`, the webserver's `inject`) merge from the official row.
# The `connection` override restates `inject` to add `settings` so the loader
# only evaluates its expressions once the settings service exists (inject is
# the loader's activation gate for expression dependencies).
#
# Both expressions fail closed: any evaluation error yields the official
# defaults (loopback bind, the deployment fence) and never fails the boot.

- insert:
    - id: lan-access
      name: 'dsh-lan-access'
      inject: [settings, loader]

# ── static bind + fence overrides (evaluated once per boot) ─────────────────

- id: webserver
  inject: [webStartup, settings]
  config:
    # Loopback while the lan-access entry is disabled (the market toggle
    # state, composed before activation) or while the settings-tab toggle
    # is off; all interfaces only when both say enabled.
    host: !!js (() => { try { const lan = [...ctx.loader.entries()].find((e) => e.options.id === "lan-access"); if (lan?.disabled ?? true) return ctx.webStartup?.host ?? "127.0.0.1"; const raw = ctx.get("settings").section("lan-access"); if (!(raw !== null && typeof raw === "object" && raw.enabled === true)) return ctx.webStartup?.host ?? "127.0.0.1"; return "0.0.0.0"; } catch { return ctx.webStartup?.host ?? "127.0.0.1"; } })()
    port: !!js ctx.webStartup.port ?? 3080
    compression: gzip
    compressionLevel: 1
    compressionThresholdBytes: 1024

- id: connection
  inject: [webRuntime, settings]
  config:
    # While enabled (entry not disabled AND settings-tab toggle on): the
    # configured accessHosts (canonical form only) ARE the policy — with a
    # non-empty configuration nothing else passes the fence; the
    # deployment-derived webRuntime.trustedHosts is only the fallback for
    # an empty configuration. While disabled: the official expression
    # untouched.
    trustedHosts: !!js (() => { try { const lan = [...ctx.loader.entries()].find((e) => e.options.id === "lan-access"); if (lan?.disabled ?? true) return ctx.webRuntime.trustedHosts; const raw = ctx.get("settings").section("lan-access"); if (!(raw !== null && typeof raw === "object" && raw.enabled === true)) return ctx.webRuntime.trustedHosts; let list = []; if (Array.isArray(raw.accessHosts)) list = raw.accessHosts; const out = []; const seen = new Set(); for (const h of list) { if (typeof h !== "string" || seen.has(h.toLowerCase())) continue; try { const u = new URL("http://" + h); let port = u.port; if (port === "") port = new URL("https://" + h).port; let canon = u.hostname; if (port !== "") canon = canon + ":" + port; if (canon !== h.toLowerCase()) continue; } catch { continue; } seen.add(h.toLowerCase()); out.push(h); } if (out.length > 0) return out; return ctx.webRuntime.trustedHosts; } catch { return ctx.webRuntime.trustedHosts; } })()
    # The configured browser-session lifetime while enabled (entry not
    # disabled AND settings-tab toggle on); the official default (30)
    # while disabled or unconfigured.
    cookieMaxAgeDays: !!js (() => { try { const lan = [...ctx.loader.entries()].find((e) => e.options.id === "lan-access"); if (lan?.disabled ?? true) return 30; const raw = ctx.get("settings").section("lan-access"); if (!(raw !== null && typeof raw === "object" && raw.enabled === true)) return 30; const days = raw.sessionDays; if (Number.isSafeInteger(days)) return Math.min(Math.max(days, 1), 3650); return 30; } catch { return 30; } })()

readme.text:
> **Who this is for**: users who already run a virtual LAN (EasyTier / Tailscale / WireGuard / ZeroTier …), or who only want to reach the dsh Web UI from a trusted LAN (home or office network).
>
> **⚠️ Security**: enabling LAN access means *anyone who can reach that address can operate your Harness — remote code execution exposed to that network segment*. Only enable it on a network you control; never on public Wi-Fi, campus or shared lab networks. Never forward the token-bearing URL printed at startup.
>
> **🤖 About this repository**: every line of code, doc, and commit here was generated by an AI coding agent; the author has not reviewed it line by line. Read `cordis.patch.yml` and `lib/client.js` (they touch dsh internals) before you rely on it. Issues and PRs welcome.

Open the DeepSeek Harness Web GUI's LAN access fences so other machines on a
(virtual) LAN can reach it directly via `LAN-IP:port`, with a settings tab to
choose which LAN IP is used.

See `README.zh.md` (Chinese) for the full guide; the English summary:

- **What it changes**: binds the webserver to `0.0.0.0` when enabled (the host
  schema only allows `127.0.0.1` / `0.0.0.0`), makes the `/api` browser-trust
  fence accept **only** your configured authorities (falling back to dsh's
  automatic LAN trust when you configure none), and prints the token-bearing
  LAN URL at boot.
- **Strict fence (0.2.0, breaking)**: dsh itself trusts every non-internal IPv4
  while the server binds `0.0.0.0`; 0.1.x unioned that in, so a host you removed
  stayed trusted. Since 0.2.0 a non-empty configuration *is* the policy.
- **Remote (non-loopback) visits**: dsh runs its settings layer in memory mode
  there, so nothing can be read or persisted. The plugin shadows the shipped
  welcome notice and repairs the settings mirror; opt out of the latter with
  `rescueSettings: false` in the `lan-access` section of `settings.yaml`.
- **Session lifetime**: `sessionDays` (default 30, range 1–3650) sets how long a
  device stays authenticated after one token visit. Cookies are per access
  address and survive a `dsh web` restart (the signing secret is persisted);
